families.summary: The native app has a real shared School mode runtime. It uses a bounded version-1 record in %LOCALAPPDATA%/DingDing/SharedPresentation/school-mode-v1.json, guarded by a lock-file compare-and-swap, with a 500 ms poll plus a filesystem watcher. It fails closed until the record is read. The unlock credential lives in the OS vault under a shared account with an attempt budget. A Preferences control can rename the mode, set or replace the credential, enable it, and unlock-and-disable it, and includes the honest 'not a security boundary' disclosure. While the mode is on, suppression is applied to the language mode, funny levels, bilingual decorator, personal vocabulary, the Cantonese narrator, settings teleport, and palette preference rows. Several required parts are missing. Dim-sum surfaces are not suppressed: changelog code names, the release splash art, the surprise display path, and the palette document entries for codenames and splash art. The offline documentation viewer still offers Cantonese and bilingual articles and dim-sum articles, and its bundled text reveals the shipped name. Open surfaces (the modal Preferences, palette, docs, changelog) are not rebuilt live; most suppression is decided once, when the dialog is built. There is no passkey choice. Status copy uses generic wording instead of the chosen name. The control's strings are not in the Cantonese catalogue. The emoji switch is suppressed even though the contract does not list it. The School unlock lockout has no unlock ladder. The local-capability bridge registers no school.state or school.manage handlers. The public site has no School mode. There is no user-facing article and no .yue_HK twin. Only service-level tests and no built-app captures exist.

families.summary: Main compiles and runs two independent scheduled-settings engines at the same time, with separate stores, different precedence, and conflicting semantics. Engine A (src/slic3r/GUI/Schedule, Preferences > Schedules) stores rules in AppConfig 'scheduled_settings' and supports 9 keys with list-order precedence. It applies values by writing them permanently into AppConfig base settings and keeps a separate captured-base map. It reads the 'live' value through AppConfig::get, which returns School-suppressed or overlay values, so it can capture and later permanently write a suppressed or scheduled value as the user's base. It reads the Home Assistant token from plaintext 'ha_token' in the config and has no private-address or DNS-rebinding protection. Its language changes only take effect after restart, and its rule editor offers Cantonese, bilingual and funny-level values even under School mode. Engine B (libslic3r/ScheduledSettings plus FeatureServices::ScheduledPreferences, File > Scheduled settings) is the stronger design: a strict schema, priority then order, a nonpersistent EffectivePreferences overlay, a vault-stored Home Assistant token, DNS-pinned curl with no redirects and bounded size and time, a history snapshot, a timezone list, and School-aware key filtering. However, its 'Add rule' seeds the unregistered key 'theme', so a new rule can never validate or save. Its strings bypass the catalogue (the translate callback drops the inline Cantonese). Its failure notice carries no recovery action and fires only for two states. It uses raw wx controls. Neither engine covers every appearance or customization value (element styles, logo, font weight and others). Neither is in Export everything. Engine B's tests are not in CTest, and Engine A has no tests. The two documentation articles contradict each other, and the Engine B README has no Cantonese twin. The public site has a local-only rule engine with 13 source tests; its API and Home Assistant sources are shown as unavailable.

families.summary: Preferences (Appearance page) always shows a Personal vocabulary box, except under School mode. It has Load/Replace JSON, a Clear button, a semantic wxFileDialog picker, and localized no-file, loaded and invalid status text. The parser enforces schema version 1, a 1 MiB limit, depth 3, 2048 entries and 512-byte strings. It rejects duplicate and unsafe keys and unknown fields, and never applies a rejected file partially. The validated cache is written atomically to a private local app-data folder that stores no source path. Replacements are applied only at display adapters (Label painting, Button including its accessible name, DropDown, MD3Menu, canvas menu labels, SurfaceRegistry), and the profile export skips the cache path. Five things are missing. The palette has no vocabulary entries. Label accessible names, native wx controls, tooltips, window titles, notifications and general ImGui text bypass the transform. Embedded WebView2 pages have neither the control nor the transform. Exports and history views do not say that vocabulary data was omitted. Tests cover only parsing and bounds. families.summary: The narrator is off by default (narrator_enabled=false) and uses a SAPI late-bound backend. A completion-driven serialized queue speaks English then Cantonese for 'Both', applies a 20-second per-category cooldown, replaces queued lines of the same category, and lets errors bypass the cooldown. It yields to a screen reader (SPI_GETSCREENREADER, polled each second), has a quiet toggle, and shuts down cleanly. Preferences > Other has separate English and Cantonese voice pickers with an Automatic default, stable SAPI token IDs, retained missing selections, an effective-voice status line, per-language rate and pitch from -10 to 10, re-enumeration every 2 seconds, an external-mirror label and palette entries. Seven gaps remain. Only printer state and error changes plus the filament-scanner preview are narrated; slicing, export, update and app error events are not. SAPI-only enumeration misses the OneCore and natural voices where Hong Kong Cantonese voices normally live. Narrator settings copy has no Cantonese translation. Windows quiet hours are not respected. Tone ignores the funny level because narration lines have no ladders. Legacy say() and say_now() follow the interface language. The narration article has no Cantonese twin, and there are no tests for rate and pitch bounds, missing synthesis or every language mode.

families.summary: Audited at HEAD 45b0a9ec9. That is two commits after 38c76dfd, and those commits only add a screenshot workflow and regenerate the docs bundle, so no converter code changed. The native converter has a strong core. It has a documented registry covering all eight required categories. Adapters stay disabled until the bundled worker passes a SHA-256 check and a live capability probe, and unavailable formats (extended images, audio, video, multi-entry archives, office, DOCX/EPUB) stay visible with exact reasons. Conversions run in a zero-capability AppContainer worker under a job object (one process, 256 MiB, 30 s) with no PATH, shell or network. Every output is validated before an atomic no-replace publish that re-reads the source. Seven qpdf 12.4.2 PDF operations are hash-pinned, and the durable paged queue has no total cap, persistent pause/resume/cancel, crash-to-recovery-required handling and a storage preflight. The panel is reachable from File > Local file converter in the Local tools tab. The user-facing surface falls short of the contract in several ways. It is built from raw wx controls (wxNotebook, wxListCtrl, wxTextCtrl) rather than registered MD3 primitives. It has no Cantonese or bilingual translations, and adapter names, disclosures, reasons, states and result codes are untranslatable English from libslic3r. Lossy changes are disclosed but never explicitly acknowledged. The only preview is a kind-and-byte-count status line. Bulk actions cover only the current page. The PDF metadata tool edits only Title. There is no open-output or editor action, no notification integration and no funny levels. PDF is known to fail initialization inside the AppContainer (USER32 1114) in the verification context. No focused test runs in CI. The Pages site and the embedded web pages have no converter surface. Audio and Video have no enabled adapters; they are honestly disabled, which meets the letter of the contract but leaves those categories with no working conversion.
